title: Remote Pilot (Part 107)
note: Questions and choices are reproduced from the FAA sample-question document (a U.S. Government work). The FAA document has no answer key: answers and explanations are written by OpenChecklists and cite FAA sources.

questions.stem: What are characteristics of a moist, unstable air mass?
questions.explanation: Moist, unstable air rises readily, producing cumuliform clouds, turbulence and showery precipitation, usually with good visibility outside the showers.

cites.label: Pilot's Handbook of Aeronautical Knowledge (FAA-H-8083-25C), ch. 12, Weather Theory

questions.stem: According to 14 CFR part 107, how may a remote pilot operate an unmanned aircraft in Class C airspace?

choices.A: The remote pilot must have prior authorization from the Air Traffic Control (ATC) facility having jurisdiction over that airspace.
choices.B: The remote pilot must monitor the Air Traffic Control (ATC) frequency from launch to recovery.
choices.C: The remote pilot must contact the Air Traffic Control (ATC) facility after launching the unmanned aircraft.

questions.explanation: Part 107 prohibits operating in Class B, C or D airspace, or in the surface area of Class E designated for an airport, without prior authorization from ATC.

questions.stem: According to 14 CFR part 107 the remote pilot in command (PIC) of a small unmanned aircraft planning to operate within Class C airspace

choices.B: is required to file a flight plan.
choices.C: is required to receive ATC authorization.

questions.explanation: Operations in Class C airspace require prior ATC authorization. A visual observer and a flight plan are not required.

questions.stem: What effect does high density altitude have on the efficiency of a UA propeller?

choices.C: Density altitude does not affect propeller efficiency.

questions.explanation: High density altitude means thinner air. The propeller has less air to work with, so it produces less thrust and propeller efficiency decreases.

cites.label: Pilot's Handbook of Aeronautical Knowledge (FAA-H-8083-25C), p. 4-4, Principles of Flight

questions.stem: (Refer to FAA-CT-8080-2H, Figure 22, area 2.) At Coeur D`Alene which frequency should be used as a Common Traffic Advisory Frequency (CTAF) to monitor airport traffic?
questions.explanation: The circled C next to 122.8 in the Coeur d'Alene data block marks it as the CTAF. 135.075 is the AWOS.

questions.stem: Which technique should a remote pilot use to scan for traffic? A remote pilot should

choices.A: systematically focus on different segments of the sky for short intervals.
choices.B: concentrate on relative movement detected in the peripheral vision area.
choices.C: continuously scan the sky from right to left.

questions.explanation: Effective scanning uses a series of short, regularly spaced eye movements, briefly focusing on each segment of the sky.

cites.label: Pilot's Handbook of Aeronautical Knowledge (FAA-H-8083-25C), p. 14-28, Airport Operations

questions.stem: (Refer to FAA-CT-8080-2H, Figure 2.) If an unmanned airplane weighs 33 pounds, what approximate weight would the airplane structure be required to support during a 30° banked turn while maintaining altitude?
questions.explanation: At 30° of bank in level flight the load factor is 1.154 G, so the structure must support 33 × 1.154 ≈ 38 pounds.

cites.label: Pilot's Handbook of Aeronautical Knowledge (FAA-H-8083-25C), ch. 5, Aerodynamics of Flight

questions.stem: (Refer to FAA-CT-8080-2H, Figure 23, area 3.) What is the floor of the Savannah Class C airspace at the shelf area (outer circle)?
questions.explanation: The outer circle of Savannah Class C is labeled 41/13: ceiling 4,100 feet MSL, floor 1,300 feet MSL. Class C altitudes on sectionals are in MSL.

questions.stem: (Refer to FAA-CT-8080-2H, Figure 20, area 3.) With ATC authorization, you are operating your small unmanned aircraft approximately 4 SM southeast of Elizabeth City Regional Airport (ECG). What hazard is indicated to be in that area?

choices.A: High density military operations in the vicinity.
choices.B: Unmarked balloon on a cable up to 3,008 feet AGL.
choices.C: Unmarked balloon on a cable up to 3,008 feet MSL.

questions.explanation: The caution box warns of an unmarked balloon on a cable up to 3,008 feet MSL. Charted altitudes are MSL unless marked otherwise.

questions.stem: The most comprehensive information on a given airport is provided by

choices.A: the Chart Supplements U.S. (formerly Airport Facility Directory).

questions.explanation: The Chart Supplement U.S. (formerly the Airport/Facility Directory) provides the most comprehensive information on a given airport.

cites.label: Pilot's Handbook of Aeronautical Knowledge (FAA-H-8083-25C), p. 14-3, Airport Operations

questions.stem: Identify the hazardous attitude or characteristic a remote pilot displays while taking risks in order to impress others?
questions.explanation: Taking risks to impress others is the macho attitude ("I can do it"). Its antidote is "Taking chances is foolish."

cites.label: Pilot's Handbook of Aeronautical Knowledge (FAA-H-8083-25C), p. 2-5, Aeronautical Decision-Making

questions.stem: (Refer to FAA-CT-8080-2H, Figure 26, area 4.) You have been hired to inspect the tower under construction at 46.9N and 98.6W, near Jamestown Regional (JMS). What must you receive prior to flying your unmanned aircraft in this area?

choices.C: Authorization from the National Park Service.

questions.explanation: The site is inside the Jamestown Class E surface area (dashed magenta line). Part 107 requires ATC authorization in Class E airspace designated for an airport.

questions.stem: (Refer to FAA-CT-8080-2H, Figure 20, area 5.) How would a remote PIC "CHECK NOTAMS" as noted in the CAUTION box regarding the unmarked balloon?

choices.A: By utilizing the B4UFLY mobile application.
choices.B: By contacting the FAA district office.
choices.C: By obtaining a briefing via an online source such as: 1800WXBrief.com.

questions.explanation: NOTAMs are available through a flight service briefing, including online services such as 1800wxbrief.com.

questions.stem: When adapting crew resource management (CRM) concepts to the operation of a small UA, CRM must be integrated into
questions.explanation: Crew resource management applies to every phase of the operation, from planning and preflight through recovery and debrief.

cites.label: Pilot's Handbook of Aeronautical Knowledge (FAA-H-8083-25C), p. 2-4, Aeronautical Decision-Making

questions.stem: You have been hired as a remote pilot by a local TV news station to film breaking news with a small UA. You expressed a safety concern and the station manager has instructed you to `fly first, ask questions later.` What type of hazardous attitude does this attitude represent?
questions.explanation: "Fly first, ask questions later" is the impulsive attitude ("Do it quickly"). Its antidote is "Not so fast. Think first."

cites.label: Pilot's Handbook of Aeronautical Knowledge (FAA-H-8083-25C), p. 2-5, Aeronautical Decision-Making

questions.stem: A local TV station has hired a remote pilot to operate their small UA to cover news stories. The remote pilot has had multiple near misses with obstacles on the ground and two small UAS accidents. What would be a solution for the news station to improve their operating safety culture?

choices.A: The news station should implement a policy of no more than five crashes/incidents within 6 months.
choices.B: The news station does not need to make any changes; there are times that an accident is unavoidable.
choices.C: The news station should recognize hazardous attitudes and situations and develop standard operating procedures that emphasize safety.

questions.explanation: A healthy safety culture recognizes hazardous attitudes and situations and sets standard operating procedures that put safety first. Accepting accidents or setting crash quotas does the opposite.

cites.label: Pilot's Handbook of Aeronautical Knowledge (FAA-H-8083-25C), p. 2-5, Aeronautical Decision-Making
Pilot's Handbook of Aeronautical Knowledge (FAA-H-8083-25C), ch. 2, Aeronautical Decision-Making

questions.stem: (Refer to FAA-CT-8080-2H, Figure 26, area 2.) While monitoring the Cooperstown CTAF you hear an aircraft announce that they are midfield left downwind to RWY 13. Where would the aircraft be relative to the runway?
questions.explanation: Left traffic for runway 13 puts the downwind leg on the left of the landing direction (130°), which is the northeast side. An aircraft at midfield left downwind is therefore east of the runway.

questions.stem: To avoid a possible collision with a manned airplane, you estimate that your small UA climbed to an altitude greater than 600 feet AGL. To whom must you report the deviation?

choices.C: Upon request of the Federal Aviation Administration.

questions.explanation: A remote pilot who deviates from Part 107 in an in-flight emergency must send a written report of the deviation to the FAA, but only upon request.

questions.stem: When operating an unmanned airplane, the remote pilot should consider that the load factor on the wings may be increased any time

choices.A: the CG is shifted rearward to the aft CG limit.
choices.B: the airplane is subjected to maneuvers other than straight-and-level flight.

questions.explanation: Load factor increases whenever the aircraft is maneuvered out of straight-and-level flight, for example in turns, pull-ups or gusts.

cites.label: Pilot's Handbook of Aeronautical Knowledge (FAA-H-8083-25C), ch. 5, Aerodynamics of Flight

questions.stem: A stall occurs when the smooth airflow over the unmanned airplane`s wing is disrupted and the lift degenerates rapidly. This is caused when the wing

choices.C: exceeds its critical angle of attack.

questions.explanation: A stall occurs when the wing exceeds its critical angle of attack, regardless of speed or weight.

cites.label: Pilot's Handbook of Aeronautical Knowledge (FAA-H-8083-25C), p. 5-3, Aerodynamics of Flight

questions.stem: Safety is an important element for a remote pilot to consider prior to operating an unmanned aircraft system. To prevent the final "link" in the accident chain, a remote pilot must consider which methodology?
questions.explanation: Accidents are rarely one event; they are a chain of decisions and events. The Risk Management Handbook identifies inadequate risk management as the common thread, so identifying hazards and managing risk is how a pilot breaks the chain before its final link.

cites.label: Pilot's Handbook of Aeronautical Knowledge (FAA-H-8083-25C), p. 2-12, Aeronautical Decision-Making

questions.stem: You are a remote pilot for a co-op energy service provider. You are to use your UA to inspect power lines in a remote area 15 hours away from your home office. After the drive, fatigue impacts your abilities to complete your assignment on time. Fatigue can be recognized

choices.B: as being in an impaired state.
choices.C: by an ability to overcome sleep deprivation.

questions.explanation: Fatigue is an impairment. It degrades attention, concentration, coordination and communication, and often goes unnoticed by the pilot until errors are made.

questions.stem: (Refer to FAA-CT-8080-2H, Figure 21.) What airport is located approximately 47 (degrees) 40 (minutes) N latitude and 101 (degrees) 26 (minutes) W longitude?
questions.explanation: Plotting 47°40'N, 101°26'W (20 minutes south of 48° N and 26 minutes west of 101° W) lands on Garrison airport.

questions.stem: (Refer to FAA-CT-8080-2H, Figure 12.) What are the current conditions for Chicago Midway Airport (KMDW)?

choices.B: Sky 7,000 feet overcast, visibility 1-1/2SM, heavy rain.
choices.C: Sky 700 feet overcast, visibility 11, occasionally 2SM, with rain.

questions.explanation: SPECI KMDW ... 1 1/2SM RA OVC007 decodes as visibility 1-1/2 statute miles in rain, overcast ceiling at 700 feet.

questions.stem: (Refer to FAA-CT-8080-2H, Figure 12.) The wind direction and velocity at KJFK is from
questions.explanation: 18004KT means wind from 180° true at 4 knots. METAR wind directions are referenced to true north.

cites.label: Pilot's Handbook of Aeronautical Knowledge (FAA-H-8083-25C), ch. 13, Aviation Weather Services

questions.stem: According to 14 CFR part 107, what is required to operate a small UA within 30 minutes after official sunset?

choices.B: Must be operated in a rural area.

questions.explanation: During civil twilight (30 minutes before sunrise or after sunset) the small UA needs lighted anti-collision lighting visible for at least 3 statute miles.

questions.stem: To ensure that the unmanned aircraft center of gravity (CG) limits are not exceeded, follow the aircraft loading instructions specified in the

choices.A: Pilot`s Operating Handbook or UAS Flight Manual.

questions.explanation: Loading and CG limits for a specific aircraft come from that aircraft's Pilot's Operating Handbook or UAS flight manual.

cites.label: Pilot's Handbook of Aeronautical Knowledge (FAA-H-8083-25C), ch. 10, Weight and Balance

questions.stem: According to 14 CFR part 107, who is responsible for determining the performance of a small unmanned aircraft?
questions.explanation: The remote pilot in command is directly responsible for the operation and must complete the preflight assessment, including making sure there is enough power and performance for the intended flight.

questions.stem: (Refer to FAA-CT-8080-2H, Figure 59, area 2.) The chart shows a gray line with "VR1667, VR1617, VR1638, and VR1668." Could this area present a hazard to the operations of a small UA?

choices.A: No, all operations will be above 400 feet.
choices.B: Yes, this is a Military Training Route from the surface to 1,500 feet AGL.
choices.C: Yes, the defined route provides traffic separation to manned aircraft.

questions.explanation: VR routes with four-digit numbers are military training routes flown at or below 1,500 feet AGL, which includes the altitudes where small UA operate.

questions.stem: (Refer to FAA-CT-8080-2H, Figure 26.) What does the line of latitude at area 4 measure?

choices.A: The degrees of latitude east and west of the Prime Meridian.
choices.B: The degrees of latitude north and south of the equator.
choices.C: The degrees of latitude east and west of the line that passes through Greenwich, England.

questions.explanation: Lines of latitude (parallels) measure degrees north and south of the equator. Longitude measures east and west of the Prime Meridian.

cites.label: Pilot's Handbook of Aeronautical Knowledge (FAA-H-8083-25C), ch. 16, Navigation

questions.stem: Under what condition should the operator of a small UA establish scheduled maintenance protocol?

choices.A: When the manufacturer does not provide a maintenance schedule.
choices.B: UAS does not need a required maintenance schedule.
choices.C: When the FAA requires you to, following an accident.

questions.explanation: If the manufacturer gives no maintenance schedule, the operator should set up a scheduled maintenance protocol. Part 107 still requires the UAS to be in a condition for safe operation.

questions.stem: According to 14 CFR part 107, the responsibility to inspect the small UAS to ensure it is in a safe operating condition rests with the
questions.explanation: Before each flight the remote pilot in command must check the small UAS to determine whether it is in a condition for safe operation.

questions.stem: According to 14 CFR part 48, when would a small UA owner not be permitted to register it?

choices.A: If the owner is less than 13 years of age.
choices.B: All persons must register their small UA.
choices.C: If the owner does not have a valid United States driver`s license.

questions.explanation: A small UA must be registered by its owner, unless the owner is under 13. In that case someone at least 13 years old must register it.

questions.stem: Which is true regarding the presence of alcohol within the human body?

choices.A: A small amount of alcohol increases vision acuity.
choices.B: Consuming an equal amount of water will increase the destruction of alcohol and alleviate a hangover.
choices.C: Judgment and decision-making abilities can be adversely affected by even small amounts of alcohol.

questions.explanation: Even small amounts of alcohol impair judgment and decision-making. Water does not speed the elimination of alcohol from the body.

cites.label: Pilot's Handbook of Aeronautical Knowledge (FAA-H-8083-25C), p. 17-15, Aeromedical Factors

questions.stem: When using a small UA in a commercial operation, who is responsible for briefing the participants about emergency procedures?
questions.explanation: The remote PIC must make sure everyone directly participating is briefed on operating conditions, emergency and contingency procedures, roles and hazards.

questions.stem: What are the characteristics of stable air?
questions.explanation: Stable air resists vertical motion. It typically brings stratiform clouds, smooth air, poor visibility and steady precipitation.

cites.label: Pilot's Handbook of Aeronautical Knowledge (FAA-H-8083-25C), ch. 12, Weather Theory

questions.stem: You have received an outlook briefing from flight service through 1800wxbrief.com. The briefing indicates you can expect a low-level temperature inversion with high relative humidity. What weather conditions would you expect?

choices.A: Smooth air, poor visibility, fog, haze, or low clouds.
choices.B: Light wind shear, poor visibility, haze, and light rain.
choices.C: Turbulent air, poor visibility, fog, low stratus type clouds, and showery precipitation.

questions.explanation: Inversions are layers of smooth, stable air that trap moisture and pollutants beneath them. With high relative humidity, expect smooth air with poor visibility in fog, haze or low clouds.

cites.label: Pilot's Handbook of Aeronautical Knowledge (FAA-H-8083-25C), p. 12-13, Weather Theory

questions.stem: When may a remote pilot reduce the intensity of an aircraft’s lights during a night flight?

choices.A: At no time may the lights of an sUAS be reduced in intensity at night.
choices.B: When a manned aircraft is in the vicinity of the sUAS.
choices.C: When it is in the interest of safety to dim the aircraft's lights.

questions.explanation: The remote PIC may reduce the intensity of the anti-collision lighting, but never turn it off, when operating conditions make that safer.

questions.stem: What must a person, who is manipulating the controls of a small unmanned aircraft, do if the standard remote identification fails during a flight?

choices.A: Land the aircraft as soon as practicable.
choices.B: Notify the nearest FAA Air Traffic facility.

questions.explanation: If a standard remote identification aircraft stops broadcasting, the person manipulating the controls must land as soon as practicable.

questions.stem: Where must a small unmanned aircraft’s serial number be listed when using either standard remote identification or a broadcast module?
questions.explanation: The serial number of a standard remote ID aircraft, or of the broadcast module, must be listed on the aircraft's Certificate of Aircraft Registration.

questions.stem: When preparing for a night flight, what should an sUAS pilot be aware of after assembling and conducting a preflight of an aircraft while using a bright flashlight or work light?

choices.A: Once adapted to darkness, a persons eyes are relatively immune to bright lights.
choices.B: It takes approximately 30 minutes for a persons eyes to fully adapt to darkness.
choices.C: The person should use a flash light equipped with LED lights to facilitate their night vision.

questions.explanation: Full dark adaptation takes about 30 minutes, and a moment of bright light can undo it. Use dim or red light after preflighting under bright light.

cites.label: Pilot's Handbook of Aeronautical Knowledge (FAA-H-8083-25C), ch. 17, Aeromedical Factors

questions.stem: To conduct Category 1 operations, a remote pilot in command must use a small unmanned aircraft that weighs
questions.explanation: Category 1 operations over people require a small UA that weighs 0.55 pounds or less, including everything on board, with no exposed rotating parts that would lacerate skin.

questions.stem: Which Category of small unmanned aircraft must have an airworthiness certificate issued by the FAA?
questions.explanation: Category 4 small UA must have an airworthiness certificate issued under part 21.

questions.stem: Your surveying company is a title sponsor for a race team at the Indianapolis 500. To promote your new aerial surveying department, you decide to video part of the race using a small UA. The FAA has issued a Temporary Flight Restriction (TFR) for the race in the area you plan to fly. In this situation

choices.A: you may fly your drone in the TFR since your company is sponsoring a team at the race.
choices.B: the TFR applies to all aircraft; you may not fly in the area without a Certificate of Waiver or Authorization.
choices.C: flying your drone is allowed if you notify all non-participating people of the closed course UA operation.

questions.explanation: Remote pilots must comply with TFRs (§§ 91.137–91.145 and 99.7). Sponsorship gives no exemption, so you may not fly in the TFR without the specific authorization or waiver the restriction requires.

skipped.stem: (Refer to FAA-CT-8080-2H, Figure 21.) You have been hired by a farmer to use your small UA to inspect his crops. The area that you are to survey is in the Devil`s Lake West MOA, east of area 2. How would you find out if the MOA is active?
skipped.reason: Ambiguous: the FAA's guidance (AIM 3-4-5) is to contact flight service or the controlling agency for MOA status; none of the choices clearly matches that.

skipped.stem: According to 14 CFR part 48, when must a person register a small UA with the Federal Aviation Administration?
skipped.reason: Ambiguous under current 14 CFR 48.15: both A and B describe situations where registration is required.
